run.question: We're getting mapping errors and slow indexing on our events index. Can you check the field mappings for our app-188-index-* indexes and tell me if any have an unusually high number of fields? What's the exact field count for each?

report.summary: Mappings were read for all four indices matching app-188-index-*. Exact top-level field counts: app-188-index-a = 10, app-188-index-b = 10, app-188-index-c = 10, app-188-index-x = 523. app-188-index-x is the outlier by a wide margin: its 523 fields are all leaf fields and consist of @timestamp, event_type, user_id plus 130 metric_* fields, 130 flag_* fields, 130 label_* fields and 130 counter_* fields (type spread: 132 text, 131 long, 130 boolean, 129 float, 1 date). app-188-index-a, -b and -c share one identical 10-field event schema (@timestamp date, action keyword, duration_ms integer, error_message text, event_type keyword, ip_address ip, metadata object, session_id keyword, status keyword, user_id keyword). A concrete schema divergence also exists: in app-188-index-x, event_type and user_id are text with a .keyword sub-field, whereas in a/b/c both are plain keyword, and x lacks action, duration_ms, error_message, ip_address, metadata, session_id and status. Data volume is not the anomaly: x holds 1 document (204.4kb) and a/b/c hold 0 documents (227b each), all four green and open. Whether x's 523-field mapping or the type divergence is what produces the reported mapping errors and slow indexing is not established by this evidence; no index statistics, mapping-exception or Elasticsearch log data was reachable, so causation remains a hypothesis.

claims.text: Four indices match app-188-index-* : app-188-index-a, app-188-index-b, app-188-index-c (each 0 documents, 227b primary store) and app-188-index-x (1 document, 204.4kb primary store); all four are health green and status open.
Exact top-level field counts: app-188-index-a = 10, app-188-index-b = 10, app-188-index-c = 10, app-188-index-x = 523.
app-188-index-x's 523 fields are all leaf fields (no field carries nested properties), and its mapping does not declare dynamic, date_detection or numeric_detection.

The field names in app-188-index-x are generated families: @timestamp, event_type, user_id, plus 130 counter_* fields, 130 metric_* fields, 130 flag_* fields and 130 label_* fields (examples counter_0001, metric_0000, flag_0002, label_0003).
Type distribution of app-188-index-x's fields: 132 text, 131 long, 130 boolean, 129 float, 1 date.

app-188-index-a, -b and -c have the identical 10-field mapping: @timestamp date, action keyword, duration_ms integer, error_message text, event_type keyword, ip_address ip, metadata object, session_id keyword, status keyword, user_id keyword.

Schema divergence between app-188-index-x and its siblings: in app-188-index-x, event_type and user_id are mapped as text with a keyword sub-field (ignore_above 256) and @timestamp is date, whereas in a/b/c event_type and user_id are plain keyword; app-188-index-x also has none of the fields action, duration_ms, error_message, ip_address, metadata, session_id or status.
None of the four app-188-index-* indices carries an alias.
A listing of all indices that do not match app-188 returned no entries, so in this Elasticsearch the app-188-index-* set is the only set of indices visible to the query.
The sibling indices are not bloated: app-188-index-a, -b and -c each map only 10 fields with a conventional event schema, so the anomalously high field count is confined to app-188-index-x.

Rejected as the cause of slow indexing on data volume: app-188-index-x holds only 1 document (204.4kb) and the other three hold 0 documents, so mapping size rather than stored-data size is the only anomaly observed there; a large data volume is not supported by the evidence.

app-188-index-x's 523-field mapping (520 generated metric_/flag_/label_/counter_ fields, 130 of them analysed text) is a plausible contributor to slower indexing on that index, since every indexed document must resolve against that large mapping; this is not confirmed, as no index-level indexing-latency, bulk-rejection or mapping-exception data was available.

The type divergence between app-188-index-x and a/b/c on event_type and user_id (text with .keyword sub-field in x versus keyword in a/b/c) is a plausible source of the reported mapping/parse errors if the same producer writes documents into x expecting the a/b/c types, or if queries and aggregations are shared across the four indices; no error message or failed operation was observed to confirm this.

Read the index settings for app-188-index-x (index.mapping.total_fields.limit, index.mapping.depth.limit and any dynamic templates) and its Elasticsearch node logs for mapper_parsing_exception / illegal_argument_exception entries, since neither is reachable with the tools available in this Run.

Identify the producer that emits the metric_NNNN / flag_NNNN / label_NNNN / counter_NNNN field names into app-188-index-x and stop the field-per-key pattern (map them as a fixed set of key/value fields or a flattened object), then reindex or roll over to a mapping aligned with app-188-index-a/b/c.

gaps: The values of index.mapping.total_fields.limit, dynamic templates and any component/index template applied to app-188-index-* were not readable with the available tools, so whether 523 fields is near a configured limit is unknown.

No Elasticsearch indexing-latency, indexing-failure, bulk-rejection or mapper_parsing_exception data is available from this target (the only indices visible are the four app-188-index-* indices), so the reported mapping errors and slow indexing are not reproduced or quantified here.

Mapping metadata was read at query time (observed between 2026-11-21T05:05:52Z and 2026-11-21T05:06:15Z), slightly after the authorized window end of 2026-11-21T05:05:49Z; the tools have no time range, so the state of these mappings during the incident window is unknown.
The document counts shown are point-in-time index statistics, not counts inside the incident window.

Two mapping queries issued earlier in this Run failed to return data (an attempted multi-field/alias extraction expression raised a runtime error and delivered no content); only the successful retried queries are relied on above, so whether some fields carry multi-fields beyond the sampled ones remains only partially checked.

The origin of the 520 generated metric_/flag_/label_/counter_ fields (application, ingest pipeline or output configuration) is unknown; no workload, ConfigMap or Elasticsearch-side configuration tying them to a producer was inspected.
Whether any concrete document write or query actually failed on app-188-index-x is unverified; no error span, error log line or failed operation was observed for this index.
